newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche sees big rise in marketing costs.
newsitem.headline: Roche sees big rise in marketing costs.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG said it expects to significantly expand its sales organisation in line with planned new drug launches, a move that will result in a substantial rise in marketing costs.

During the current year, the company's efforts will be focused primarily on the launch of new products including a cardiovascular agent Posicor, an anti-obesity product named Xenical and a Parkinson's disease treatment called Tasmar, Roche said in an advance copy of its 1997 annual report.
"The successful launch of these innovative products will require us to significantly expand our sales organisation serving the general practitioner segment," the report said.
"We are thus responding to the increasing importance of ambulatory health care delivery," it added.
Early this year advisory panels in the United States and Europe recommended approval of Posicor for treatment of high blood pressure and angina pectoris.
In the United States Xenical qualified for the Food and Drug Administration's expedited approval procedure, Roche said.
